title: Are You 'Most Done?
author: Russell Owen
notes: The Caller's Box 2842, permission: full. The Caller's Box's own notes: "Hey can straighten out as it proceeds. Dance begins with same neighbors as in the hey." **The record is `becket-right`, and FR-C2 is why.** The transcript calls B1 "on right diagonal, hey" and names the other couple `N2`; the author's note says the dance begins with the same neighbours as the hey. Since FR-C2 a becket line slides **half** a couple width, so the two lines pass each other one couple place a time through and `N2` - the couple across the set and one couple place along the way your own couple is going - really is the couple you face next time through. The three sentences are consistent in exactly one handedness: the diagonal is on your **right** only if you progress to your right. **M9g: the two notes are one fact, and the hey carries the progression.** Straighten the right diagonal - slide each of the hey's two lines along itself until the two couples are square across the set - and each line has moved half a couple place in the direction it progresses, which *is* the becket shift. So B1's hey is written `"straighten": true` and `"progresses": true`: the lane turns under the weave over the sixteen beats, the bodies arrive where the shift reseats them, and B2 is danced with the couple you heyed with - which is the author's "dance begins with same neighbors as in the hey", one call earlier than the cycle boundary. Three mechanisms carry it (`set/heyStraightens.test.ts`, 12 cases): the schedule kind's lane is a trajectory; a dancer the call leaves on hold place slides with their own line rather than standing where a hey dancer's straightened end lands; and a couple that goes out without crossing turns half way round in its waiting hold so it steps back out on to its own two stations. **Measured, before -> after, at every checked length (4-12): `progressed` 20.0000 -> 0.0000 px**, closure 0.0000 and reach 0.0000 unchanged, collision 9.192 px at four couples and 8.277 above it -> **9.192 everywhere**. Of the three over-bound motion rows FR-C2 attributed to the boundary's walk-in, two are gone - `swing` travel 27.4 -> 21.5 and `long-lines` 24.7 -> 3.8 - and **the third did not move a digit**, so FR-C2's attribution of it is withdrawn: `allemande` travel 33.9 px/beat is B2's own card, *(4) Men allemande right 1*, a whole turn in four beats between the two larks of a becket minor set, who stand on a diagonal 37.74 px apart. Measured at six couples over beats 48-52 the lark's whole path is 73.40 px and its worst one-beat window 33.91; A1's allemande, once and a half over eight beats between the same two dancers, is 15.15, and the figure run alone is 10.1. It is the call's count, not the figure and not the boundary, and it is allowed in `motionAllowlist.ts` with that measurement in its reason - the same arithmetic the `circle` and `star` travel rows already carry. **Also measured and recorded rather than used**: `"progresses": true` on its own, with the lane left fixed, already reads `progressed` 0.0000 and green at every length; the straightening is the transcript's own note and what it buys on the numbers is collision 8.754 -> 9.192 px at five couples and up. Lisa Greenleaf's alternate B2 (#4700) is in the transcript and is not encoded.
